body_text: Flies can quickly become one of the most annoying household pests, especially during the warmer months when doors and windows stay open for longer. While chemical insect sprays may offer a quick fix, many homeowners are now looking for natural, affordable, and safer alternatives that help keep flies away without filling the house with harsh chemicals. Fortunately, there are several easy methods that use everyday kitchen ingredients to deter flies or trap them before they become a bigger problem. From roasted coffee beans to homemade vinegar traps, these simple solutions require very little effort and can help reduce unwanted insects around your home. Why Flies Enter Your Home Flies are naturally attracted to food, sweet smells, moisture, and warm environments. Leaving fruit uncovered, overflowing bins, pet food, or standing water can quickly invite flies indoors. Once inside, flies reproduce rapidly, making it important to deal with them before they become a larger nuisance. Preventing them from entering your home is often more effective than trying to eliminate them afterward. Roast Coffee Beans to Repel Flies One of the easiest natural remedies involves ordinary coffee beans. According to pest control expert Vicki Hall, roasting coffee beans in the oven releases a strong aroma that flies dislike. While many people enjoy the rich smell of freshly roasted coffee, flies tend to avoid it. To try this method: Spread whole coffee beans evenly on a baking tray. Roast them in the oven for around 10 to 15 minutes. Allow the aroma to spread naturally throughout your kitchen or living space. The pleasant coffee scent can help discourage flies from entering through open windows and doors. Some coffee shops are believed to benefit from this natural aroma, which may contribute to fewer flies being seen inside. Make an Apple Cider Vinegar Fly Trap Apple cider vinegar is another common household product that can help reduce flies indoors. Flies are attracted to the sweet fermented smell of the vinegar. By adding a few drops of washing up liquid, the liquid's surface tension is broken, making it difficult for flies to escape once they land. How to Make the Trap You only need: Apple cider vinegar A small bowl, mug, or jar A few drops of washing up liquid Pour a small amount of vinegar into the container and add several drops of washing up liquid. Place the trap near fruit bowls, kitchen counters, or windows where flies tend to gather. Over time, the trap may capture fruit flies and other small flying insects without using harmful chemicals. Create a DIY Bottle Fly Trap If you have a larger fly problem, a homemade bottle trap can be another effective option. This simple project requires only a used plastic bottle and a few household ingredients. What You Need A clean 2 litre plastic bottle Apple cider vinegar Water Scissors Instructions Remove the bottle cap. Cut the top section of the bottle approximately two to three inches below the neck. Pour a mixture of apple cider vinegar and water into the bottom half. Turn the top section upside down. Insert it into the lower half to create a funnel. Flies are attracted into the bottle through the funnel but often struggle to find their way back out. This inexpensive trap can be placed near bins, patios, kitchens, or other areas where flies frequently appear. Install Fly Screens for Long Term Protection Natural remedies work well, but preventing flies from entering your home in the first place is often the best solution. Magnetic fly screens fitted to windows allow fresh air to circulate while blocking insects from entering. These mesh screens are particularly useful during summer when windows remain open throughout the day. For homes located near gardens, parks, woodland, or farmland, fly screens can significantly reduce the number of insects indoors without affecting ventilation. Additional Ways to Reduce Flies Naturally Alongside traps and repellents, a few good household habits can make your home less attractive to flies. Keep Food Covered Avoid leaving fruit, baked goods, or leftovers uncovered on kitchen counters. Empty Bins Frequently Food waste quickly attracts flies, especially during hot weather. Regularly empty rubbish bins and clean them thoroughly. Clean Spills Promptly Sticky drink spills, crumbs, and grease can all attract insects. Wiping surfaces regularly helps reduce their food sources. Store Fruit Properly Very ripe fruit is particularly attractive to fruit flies. Refrigerating ripe fruit where appropriate can reduce infestations. Eliminate Standing Water Although houseflies mainly seek food, moisture also attracts many insects. Empty trays, buckets, or containers where water collects. Are Natural Fly Repellents Effective? Natural remedies generally work best as part of a wider prevention strategy rather than as an instant cure. Coffee bean aromas may discourage flies from entering certain areas, while vinegar traps can reduce existing fly populations over time. Results may vary depending on the severity of the infestation, the cleanliness of the home, and nearby environmental conditions. For persistent or unusually large infestations, consulting a licensed pest control professional may be the most effective solution. Final Thoughts Keeping flies out of your home does not always require expensive products or harsh chemicals. Simple household ingredients like coffee beans, apple cider vinegar, and washing up liquid can help reduce fly activity while keeping your living space more pleasant. Combined with good hygiene practices and properly fitted fly screens, these low cost methods offer an easy way to discourage flies naturally throughout the warmer months. Whether you are dealing with fruit flies in the kitchen or houseflies entering through open windows, these practical DIY techniques can help create a cleaner and more comfortable home. Disclaimer: This article is intended for informational purposes only. Natural pest control methods may produce different results depending on environmental conditions and the severity of the infestation. Always follow product safety instructions and consult a qualified pest control professional if you experience a significant or recurring pest problem.

title: Americans’ Financial Resilience Edges Lower as Recession Concerns Rise, NerdWallet’s August Financial Resilience Index Finds

body_text: Nearly two-thirds of Americans expect a recession in the next year, while more households rely on credit to manage expenses this month despite growing cash cushions SAN FRANCISCO--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Aug. 18, 2026-- NerdWallet Inc. (Nasdaq: NRDS), which provides trustworthy financial guidance to consumers and small and mid-sized businesses (SMBs), today published the August 2026 Financial Resilience Index, a monthly score that tracks how financially prepared Americans are to handle economic instability. The index edged down to 62.1 out of 100 this month, one point below July’s all-time high of 63.1. Last month's Index noted that July’s gains might not hold if global conflict escalated – a caution that proved timely, since the survey closed just before the U.S.-Iran ceasefire unraveled. By August, conditions had grown more challenging: the conflict continued, inflation stayed high, the economy shed an estimated 23,000 jobs, and consumers kept spending despite affordability constraints. “The one-point decline doesn’t signal a major shift in Americans’ financial footing, but there are signs of growing caution beneath the surface,” said Elizabeth Renter, senior economist at NerdWallet. “Household finances remain relatively resilient, even as more Americans expect a recession and many plan to rely on credit this month. The contrast between how people are managing today and what they expect tomorrow is something we’ll be watching closely.” Financial Resilience Index Three-Month Snapshot Measure August 2026 July 2026 June 2026 Financial Resilience Index Score 62.1 63.1 61.6 Feel in control of their day-to-day finances 75% 77% 76% Confident in their ability to pay all of their bills on time this month 79% 79% 78% Will rely on credit to manage at least some expenses 36% 33% 35% Have enough cash on hand to cover an unexpected $1,000 expense this month 67% 65% 63% Believe the U.S. economy will enter a recession in the next 12 months 64% 60% 62% Younger Americans Report Lower Resilience and Greater Recession Concerns Generation August 2026 FRI Score Expect a Recession Confident Paying Bills on Time Baby Boomers 72.5 58% 89% Gen Xers 62.2 61% 78% Millennials 56.8 67% 74% Gen Zers 53.8 72% 74% What We're Watching There's a growing tension in household finances: The share of Americans who can cover an unexpected $1,000 expense has risen four percentage points, from 63% in June to 67% in August, even as many expect to rely on credit, suggesting households may be growing more protective of their cash as uncertainty grows. NerdWallet will track whether that pattern continues into September and whether the gap between Americans’ current financial resilience and expectations for the economy widens. Methodology The Financial Resilience Index survey was conducted online by The Harris Poll on behalf of NerdWallet from August 4-6, 2026, among 2,086 U.S. adults ages 18 and older. The sampling precision of Harris online polls is measured by using a Bayesian credible interval. For this study, the sample data is accurate to within +/- 2.7 percentage points using a 95% confidence level. This credible interval will be wider among subsets of the surveyed population of interest. For complete survey methodology, including weighting variables and subgroup sample sizes, please contact press@nerdwallet.com . All five questions across this survey are weighted equally to develop a composite score with a maximum value of 100. As a personal finance website and app, NerdWallet provides consumers with trustworthy and knowledgeable financial information so they can make smart money moves. title: How to Find a Math Tutor in 2025
summary: Learn about how to find a math tutor in 2025, from tutoring models to learn abuot student´s needs, where to find a private math tutor to the step by step guide
body_text: Struggling to find the right math tutor? With so many options available in 2025, from traditional private tutors to AI-powered platforms, choosing the best fit for a student’s needs can be overwhelming. In this article, we will provide a comprehensive guide on how to find a math tutor, covering all the key factors you might need but could easily overlook. From understanding the importance of matching a tutor’s teaching style to your child’s learning needs to exploring the latest advancements in private tutor services, this guide will help you navigate the evolving landscape of tutoring in 2025. In-person Tutoring or Online Tutoring, Choosing the Right Mode of Tutoring In-person tutoring remains the preferred choice for young learners, who benefit from face-to-face interaction and structured learning environments. Having a tutor physically present helps with engagement, discipline, and hands-on learning, making it ideal for foundational math concepts. For more mutured and independent students, online tutoring is becoming increasingly popular. Many don’t need full-length lessons but rather targeted support, such as help with specific problems or exam preparation. Online platforms offer greater flexibility, accessibility, and making learning more efficient. Meanwhile, hybrid tutoring is emerging as a practical middle ground, combining the convenience of online sessions with the personalized touch of in-person meetings, along with advanced AI-powered tools, such as Mathos AI . This approach is ideal for students who need structured support for complex topics while maintaining the flexibility to study at their own pace. Below, we’ll break down the pros and cons of each mode to help you choose the best option. Pros Cons In-Person Tutoring - In-Person Interaction: Face-to-face communication can enhance understanding - Limited Tutor Pool: Restricted to tutors available in your local area. - Structured Environment: Traditional classroom-like settings can help students stay focused and disciplined. - Less Flexibility: Requires travel to a specific location and fixed schedules. - Immediate Feedback: Tutors can provide hands-on guidance and address questions in real time. - Higher Costs: Often more expensive due to travel and facility expenses. - No Tech Barriers: No need to worry about internet issues or device compatibility. - Time-Consuming: Commuting to and from tutoring sessions can eat into valuable time. Online Tutoring - Convenience: Learn from anywhere with an internet connection. - Lack of In-Person Interaction: May feel less personal compared to face-to-face tutoring. - Accessibility: Connect with highly qualified tutors worldwide, not limited to local options. - Technical Issues: Poor internet connectivity or device problems can disrupt sessions. - Flexibility: Schedule sessions at any time, making it easier to balance school, extracurriculars, and tutoring. - Self-Discipline Required: Students need to stay focused and motivated in a virtual environment. - Cost-Effective: Often more affordable than in-person tutoring due to reduced overhead costs. - Coverage: Easily find specialized tutors for niche topics or advanced levels. - User Feedback: Platforms often feature reviews and ratings from many users, allowing you to evaluate tutors based on feedback from other students and parents. Hybrid Tutoring - Best of Both Worlds: Combines the flexibility of online tutoring with the personal touch of in-person sessions, and AI-powered tools. - Best of Both Worlds: Combines the flexibility of online tutoring with the personal touch of in-person sessions, and AI-powered tools. - Growing Popularity: Increasingly adopted in 2025 as technology bridges the gap between online and offline learning. Understanding the Needs of the Student Now that you know the different tutoring modes available, the next step is ensuring the tutor matches the student’s specific learning needs. Every student has unique challenges, and tailoring tutoring sessions to address these is key to maximizing learning outcomes. One important factor to consider is the grade level . A child in elementary school may need a private tutor for foundational skills in reading, math, and writing, while a high school or college student might require targeted homework helper for their assignments of advanced subjects, or someone specializing in college entrance exams preparations. Whether they are preparing for the syllabus of SAT, A-Levels, GCSE, IB, AP , or completing advanced subjects, such as calculus , ensuring that the tutor is familiar with the relevant curriculum and syllabus is essential. Beyond academics, a student's learning style and tutoring objectives play a crucial role in selecting the right support. Some students need regular assistance with homework tutoring, while others seek intensive exam preparation. For those with a keen interest in subjects like mathematics, a math tutor for extracurricular tutoring classes can offer enrichment beyond school learning. Particularily, in math learning, for instance, graphing and 3D geometry might be intuitive for a visual learner but difficult for someone who learns better through hands-on activities. In such cases, using interactive graphing tools or 3D models can make a huge difference. Understanding these differences can help parents and students filter their tutoring options effectively. Step-by-Step Guide to Choosing a Private Math Tutor So much for the theory—let’s get into the practical steps of finding the right math tutor in 2025. Here’s a step-by-step guide to help you navigate the process efficiently. Step 1: Pinpoint What You Need Before reaching out to a tutor, it’s crucial for parents or students to clarify their specific needs. The more precise the answers, the easier it is to find the right match. Here are some key questions to consider: Which areas of math do you find most challenging? (e.g., algebra, calculus, geometry, statistics) Are you preparing for a specific exam? (e.g., SAT, A-Levels, IB Math, AP Calculus, national curriculum tests) Do you need help with homework, or do you want a tutor to go through the full theory of the basics? Do you prefer step-by-step explanations, visual aids, or hands-on problem-solving? Would you benefit from interactive digital tools, or do you learn better through face-to-face discussions? Having clear answers to these questions will make the search process much more efficient, helping you connect with a tutor who aligns with your learning needs faster. Step 2: Choose the Right Mode of Tutoring The student’s schedule, lifestyle, and study habits play a crucial role in deciding between online, in-person or hybrid tutoring. Online tutoring is ideal for students with packed schedules who need flexible session times. In-person tutoring works better for those who focus better in structured, face-to-face environments. Hybrid tutoring allows students to attend in-person lessons for core learning while reinforcing concepts online. For example, a student with intensive school and extracurricular commitments might find hybrid tutoring more practical—learning online during busy weeks and attending in-person lessons when extra reinforcement is needed. Step 3: Where to Find a Tutor? With so many tutoring options available, parents and students need to explore different avenues to find the best match. A. Searching for In-Person Tutors Use Google to search “math tutor near me” and check tutoring centers nearby. Visit local learning centers or libraries that offer math tutoring programs. Ask teachers, classmates, or school counselors for word-of-mouth recommendations. B. Finding Tutors Online Dedicated tutoring websites like Wyzant, Chegg Tutors, or TutorMe offer pre-vetted professionals. Freelance platforms like Fiverr, Upwork, and Preply allow students to hire independent math tutors from anywhere. Social media communities and forums (Facebook groups, Reddit, Discord) often have recommendations for top-rated tutors. Trying different platforms allows parents and students to compare tutor qualifications, pricing, reviews, and availability before making a decision. Step 4: Evaluating and Selecting the Right Tutor After shortlisting potential tutors, it’s important to assess them based on: Qualifications & experience (background in teaching, math degree, tutoring experience) Teaching style (structured lessons vs. flexible Q&A sessions) Student reviews & ratings Trial sessions (most tutors offer a free or discounted first lesson) A trial class is a great way to see whether the tutor’s teaching approach aligns with the student’s needs before committing to long-term sessions. ChatGPT or AI-powered tutoring tools? AI-powered tutoring tools have revolutionized math learning in 2025, making high-quality support more affordable, accessible, and personalized. These platforms adapt to a student’s progress, offering instant feedback, step-by-step solutions, and interactive exercises, ensuring they master concepts at their own pace. It is especially useful for self-motivated learners, students who prefer on-demand help, or those who need extra support alongside human tutoring. One of the biggest advantages is cost-effectiveness —while private tutors charge 20−20 - 20 − 100 dollars per session, online or in-person , AI tutoring tools offer subscription plans as low as 9–9– 9– 30 per month , making quality tutoring more accessible to a wider range of students. Many students today rely on AI-powered tools for math help. While ChatGPT is a great starting point, it still has limitations in solving complex equations accurately. That’s where specialized AI math tools like MathosAI come in—designed specifically for numerical precision, MathosAI boasts a 20% higher accuracy rate. Other alternatives, like Photomath and Mathway ,also offer unique features. Before subscribing, consider testing out different platforms to see which one best fits your learning style. Finding the Right Math Tutor for Success In 2025, finding a private tutor has never been more accessible, but it is not as simple as just typing "math tutor near me"into Google. The key is to identify the student’s needs, select the right mode (offline, online, or hybrid), checking tutor qualifications, and consider affordability and accessibility. Always review tutor credentials, compare pricing, and try a trial session to ensure the best fit for effective learning and academic success. By following this guide, you’ll be equipped to make the best decision for academic success. 🚀

title: Procurement compliance: Framework and best practices in 2026
summary: Learn what procurement compliance means, where it breaks down, and how intake controls, KPIs, and AI help teams prevent non-compliant spend.
body_text: Procurement compliance is a high-priority line of defense for any business. Still, failures are surprisingly common. According to Navex's 2024 State of Risk & Compliance Report , half of the respondents said their organization experienced at least one compliance issue in the past three years. When purchases occur outside of approved channels, you're exposed to a range of risks, including budget overruns, regulatory fines, and serious security vulnerabilities. A strong compliance strategy isn't just a defensive move, but a smart way to maximize value from your spending by improving efficiency and creating stronger supplier relationships. The challenge lies in the fact that modern purchasing involves multiple teams, including finance, legal, and IT. Join us as we explore what procurement compliance is, why it’s important to your organization, and how to set up a solid compliance framework. Key takeaways Procurement compliance ensures every purchase follows internal policies, external regulations, and supplier obligations. Compliance often falls apart at intake, when requests arrive through email or spreadsheets without policy checks. The strongest programs prevent issues before purchase. As Ardent Partners explains in a report on unified intake-to-pay , intake is the control point for governance, visibility, and velocity. Useful compliance KPIs include spend under management, policy exceptions, contract deviations, and audit findings. Zip enforces compliance at intake, routing requests through policy-aligned approvals, vendor checks, and spend controls before spend is committed. What is procurement compliance? Procurement compliance is the process of ensuring that every purchasing activity follows the rules that govern how an organization buys . Those rules include internal policies, external regulations, and supplier contract terms. Internal policies define how employees request purchases, which suppliers they can use, and who must approve spend. External regulations can include the Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) , the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) , the Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD) , and the Sarbanes-Oxley Act (SOX). Contractual compliance covers the obligations in signed agreements, such as pricing, delivery terms, service-level agreements (SLAs), and renewal conditions. The goal is simple: Every dollar should be authorized, policy-aligned, and auditable before the business commits to spend. Internal vs. external procurement compliance Type What it means Internal compliance Internal compliance means purchases follow company rules, including approval thresholds, budget limits, preferred supplier requirements, and conflict-of-interest policies. External compliance External compliance means purchases follow applicable laws, industry regulations, sanctions rules, data protection obligations, and sustainability reporting requirements. Internal and external compliance are connected. A regulated financial services company, for example, may need internal approval workflows that enforce DORA-related vendor checks before an information and communications technology (ICT) supplier is approved. Why procurement compliance matters Compliance directly affects procurement speed, supplier risk, and cost control . GEP reports that compliance can add 15% to 30% to procurement cycle times because of added due diligence, legal review, and security checks. The goal is not compliance despite speed, but compliance that enables speed by putting the right checks into the workflow. Strong procurement compliance helps teams reduce procurement risks before they spread downstream. When approvals, budgets, vendor screening, and contract requirements are built into the process, employees have a compliant path that is also easier to follow. It also improves spend visibility. Procurement can only manage the spend it sees, and compliance breaks down when purchases happen through side channels. Types of procurement compliance Type What it covers Policy compliance Approval rules, spend limits, supplier eligibility, and purchasing authority Supplier compliance Vendor due diligence, sanctions screening, risk checks, and supplier documentation Contract compliance Pricing, payment terms, delivery obligations, SLAs, and renewal requirements Regulatory compliance Rules such as DORA, GDPR, CSRD, SOX, and the European Union Artificial Intelligence Act (EU AI Act) Financial compliance Budget validation, purchase order controls, invoice matching, and audit records Sustainability compliance Environmental, social, and governance (ESG) reporting requirements and supplier disclosures The specific compliance requirements depend on the organization, industry, and supplier base. A public company might prioritize SOX controls, while a financial services company may need DORA-related ICT vendor oversight. A multinational buyer may need stronger CSRD and sanctions documentation. Where procurement compliance breaks down Most procurement compliance failures start at intake . When employees submit purchase requests through email or Slack, there is no reliable policy gate. The request may skip vendor validation, budget checks, approval routing, or contract review. By the time procurement sees the purchase, the business may have already chosen the supplier or committed informally. That is where maverick spend enters the picture. Maverick spend is purchasing that bypasses the approved procurement process, such as buying from an unapproved vendor or skipping required approvals. Suplari reports that maverick spend can cost organizations 5% to 16% of negotiated savings annually. The fix is simply better intake management . When purchase requests start in a structured workflow, budget validation, supplier eligibility, and approval routing can run automatically. Compliance becomes the first step instead of the cleanup step. Procurement compliance framework A practical procurement compliance framework has four stages. 1. Define the rules Start by defining the policies that govern purchasing . This includes approval thresholds, supplier eligibility rules, competitive bidding requirements, budget controls, and role-based authority. These rules should not live only in a PDF. They need to become the configuration that guides how employees request spend. 2. Embed the controls Build the rules into each stage of the procure-to-pay process . Establish budget and approval gates during intake, enforce supplier eligibility and bid requirements throughout sourcing, and prioritize clause standardization and deviation management when you reach the contracting stage. The earlier the control runs, the more useful it is. A missing approval is easy to fix before a purchase order (PO) is issued. It is harder to fix after an invoice arrives. 3. Monitor exceptions Compliance programs need real-time monitoring . Track policy exceptions, contract deviations, supplier performance issues, and spend outside approved channels. Monitoring should create an audit trail automatically. Teams need to know who approved the request, what changed, and why an exception was allowed. 4. Improve the process Use exception data and audit findings to improve the program . If one category has frequent policy exceptions, the process may be unclear, too slow, or missing the right supplier option. Compliance improves when teams treat exceptions as operating data. The pattern is more important than the one-off issue. Procurement compliance KPIs Procurement compliance needs measurement. These KPIs help teams spot gaps before auditors do. KPI What it measures Why it matters Spend under management The share of total spend governed by an approved procurement policy or contract This is the foundation. If spend under management is low, too much purchasing is happening outside approved channels. Policy exceptions by category The rate at which approved workflows are bypassed by spend category This shows where compliance is breaking down and which teams need better guidance. title: List of Forms and Contact Details Required to Request Medical Records From Cleveland Clinic
summary: Learn how attorneys can request Cleveland Clinic medical records in 2026, including verified forms, HIM contacts, addresses, processing times, and Ohio fees.
body_text: Cleveland Clinic operates a large hospital network, including its Main Campus and 15 regional hospitals in Ohio, plus five hospitals in Florida. The system uses centralized Health Information Management processes for many Ohio facilities, while Akron General and Florida facilities have separate submission instructions. For personal injury attorneys handling cases involving Cleveland Clinic treatment, navigating these workflows can create significant administrative complexity. This guide provides authorization forms, facility contacts, fee information, and submission procedures, plus how platforms like Codes Health can reduce retrieval timelines from months to a couple of weeks with AI-powered error prevention and automated provider follow-ups. Key Takeaways Cleveland Clinic uses centralized HIM processes for many Ohio facilities, while Akron General and Florida locations have separate request instructions. Standard medical record processing typically takes seven to 10 business days, while formal MyChart record requests can take up to three business days. Ohio’s 2026 maximum fees for third-party requests begin with a $24.58 records-search fee, plus applicable per-page charges and postage. Incomplete authorizations are a major source of preventable denials. Missing signatures, unclear expiration information, or incomplete sensitive-record permissions can force a request to be corrected and resubmitted. Codes Health uses AI-assisted request validation to flag issues such as misspellings, missing dates of service, and signature problems before submission. Its retrieval service averages a couple of weeks. Understanding the Basics of Medical Record Requests: What You Need to Know Medical records form the evidentiary foundation of personal injury litigation. Treatment notes can establish causation, billing records document claimed economic damages, and imaging reports can help demonstrate the nature and extent of an injury. Why Medical Records Are Essential for PI Cases Every personal injury case can depend on documentation establishing: Causation : Treatment records connecting claimed injuries with the incident Treatment progression : Ongoing care documenting the course of treatment Economic damages : Billing records supporting claimed medical expenses Pain and suffering : Treatment history, medications, referrals, and other documentation supporting the claimed impact Common Challenges in Record Retrieval Cleveland Clinic's scale creates several practical issues for law firms: Multiple facilities : Many Ohio facilities use the Cleveland Clinic’s central HIM process, while Akron General and Florida facilities have separate procedures. Facility-specific forms : Different Cleveland Clinic entities may use different authorization forms and submission routes. Processing delays : The Cleveland Clinic states that typical processing takes seven to 10 business days. Rejection loops : Authorization deficiencies may require correction and resubmission. Codes Health addresses these challenges through AI-assisted validation that reviews authorizations, date ranges, and request information before submission. Its internal materials state that the system flags preventable issues such as misspellings, missing dates of service, and signature problems. Navigating the Cleveland Clinic's Medical Records Request Process Cleveland Clinic centralizes medical records handling for many Ohio facilities, while Akron General and Cleveland Clinic Florida maintain separate request procedures. Understanding those distinctions can help prevent routing errors. Step-by-Step Guide for Cleveland Clinic Requests Step 1: Identify the correct facility Verify treatment locations through the client, medical bills, insurance EOBs, and existing records. Cleveland Clinic’s standard Ohio authorization can cover Cleveland Clinic Ohio facilities, but Akron General and Cleveland Clinic Florida use separate processes. Cases involving facilities governed by different request processes may require separate submissions. Visit the Cleveland Clinic medical records page . Step 2: Select the appropriate authorization form Ohio facilities : Use the Cleveland Clinic’s Authorization for the Release of Medical Information for covered Ohio facilities. The standard form acknowledges that released information may contain mental health, HIV/AIDS, and alcohol or drug abuse information. Psychotherapy notes require a separate authorization. Akron General : Follow Akron General’s dedicated medical-records instructions. Florida facilities : Use the applicable Cleveland Clinic Florida release form and facility-specific submission instructions. Step 3: Complete all required fields Patient's full legal name Date of birth Cleveland Clinic medical record number, if known Requested dates of service Specific records requested Recipient information Purpose of disclosure, such as legal use Required signature and date Cleveland Clinic instructs requesters to complete the applicable form, sign it, and date it before submission. Its Ohio authorization also states that the authorization expires one year from the date signed unless revoked earlier. Step 4: Attach required documentation Requirements differ by facility and circumstances: Cleveland Clinic Florida instructs requesters to include a copy of photo identification with a signature. Akron General requires photo identification for in-person record pickup. Personal representatives may need guardianship, power-of-attorney, fiduciary, executor, administrator, or other legal documentation establishing their authority. Requests involving deceased patients may require a death certificate and documentation identifying the authorized estate representative. Step 5: Submit using an accepted method Depending on the facility, Cleveland Clinic accepts combinations of: Electronic request forms MyChart requests Fax Mail Secure email at certain Florida facilities Essential Forms: Your HIPAA Medical Records Release Form Guide Proper authorization forms help reduce preventable rejection delays. Ohio Authorization Requirements Standard Authorization for Release of Medical Information Can cover the Cleveland Clinic, Ohio facilities identified on the form Requires a signature and date Expires one year after authorization unless revoked earlier Can include certain sensitive health information described in the form Psychotherapy notes require a separate authorization Cleveland Clinic also provides electronic authorization options, so the public process should not be described as universally requiring a wet signature. Florida Authorization Requirements Florida facilities provide facility-specific instructions and release forms: Weston Hospital Martin Health Indian River Hospital Find forms at Florida facilities . Cleveland Clinic Florida instructs requesters to complete all applicable fields, sign and date the authorization, and include photo identification with their signature. Completing Your Authorization Form Correctly Important information that can cause processing problems when omitted includes: Patient or authorized representative signature Signature date Specific records and dates of service requested Recipient details Required authorization for record categories governed by the applicable form An expiration date or event when required by the authorization Incomplete authorizations are the number one preventable issue Codes Health focuses on during pre-submission review. Missing signatures, unclear expiration information, or incomplete sensitive-record permissions can result in rejection and restart the provider’s processing cycle. Codes Health’s AI review flags misspellings, missing dates of service, and signature issues before submission. Codes Health also provides HIPAA-compliant electronic signatures and document-management workflows for authorization forms. Visit Codes Health . Ohio Facilities Cleveland Clinic Main Campus Contact details: Phone : 216.444.5580, Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Fax : 216.587.8043 Urgent after-hours : Call 216.444.5582 or fax 216.445.6782 after 5 p.m. and on weekends Mail : Health Information Management, Health Data Services Ab7, 9500 Euclid Avenue, Cleveland, OH 44195 More info at medical records . Visit Akron General records or submit via online form . Florida Facilities Weston Hospital Contact details: Phone : 954.689.5071 Fax : 954.689.5519 Email : roiwestonfl@ccf.org Mail : Cleveland Clinic Health Information Department, 3100 Weston Road, Weston, FL 33331 Martin Health Contact details: Phone : 772.223.5945 ext. 13070 Fax : 772.692.5140 Mail : Cleveland Clinic Martin Health Information Management (Medical Records), 200 SE Hospital Ave., Stuart, FL 34997 Indian River Hospital Contact details for Release of Information: Phone : 772.789.8479 Fax : 772.226.4101 Email : irrecordrelease@ccf.org Mail : Cleveland Clinic Indian River Hospital, Medical Records, Release of Information, 1000 36th Street, Vero Beach, FL 32960 Find Florida facility details at medical records . What to Expect After Submission Processing time : Cleveland Clinic states that typical requests generally take seven to 10 business days, depending on record availability. Delivery method : Available methods can include mail, secure email, electronic delivery, and MyChart, depending on the request and facility. Radiology imaging : Cleveland Clinic’s main medical-records guidance says to allow approximately 48 hours for radiology image requests. Indian River uses separate procedures and states three business days for radiology CDs. More at Indian River records . Accessing Your Medical Records Online: The MyChart and Portal Advantage Patient portal access through MyChart can provide a faster route for certain records when law firms coordinate appropriately with clients. Setting Up MyChart Access Cleveland Clinic's MyChart portal provides access to recent information: Registration : Available through Cleveland Clinic MyChart Record availability : Past appointment information remains visible for up to three years Formal copy processing : Cleveland Clinic says formal MyChart record requests can take up to three business days Download window : Released files remain available for 30 days Older records : Older or more detailed information should be requested from Health Information Management Benefits of Digital Record Access For law firms coordinating with clients: Patients can use the MyChart Sharing Hub to request a formal copy of their health record. Released records can be downloaded, saved, and printed for 30 days. Cleveland Clinic currently states that electronic records requested through MyChart are free. Important limitation : MyChart does not necessarily contain a patient's entire historical record. Cleveland Clinic states that past appointment information remains visible for three years, so cases requiring older baseline documentation may require a formal HIM request. Understanding HIPAA: Your Rights and Data Security HIPAA authorization and access rules affect how attorneys and patients obtain protected health information. Patient Rights Under HIPAA Individuals generally have a HIPAA right to inspect or obtain copies of protected health information in a designated record set, subject to limited exceptions. HIPAA permits reasonable, cost-based fees for access requests. For certain electronic requests, a provider may choose an optional flat-fee method of up to $6.50. The $6.50 figure is not a universal HIPAA fee cap. Cleveland Clinic currently states that electronic records requested through MyChart are free and that emailed copies cost a $6.50 flat fee plus tax. HIPAA authorizations generally identify the information being disclosed, the recipient, and other required authorization elements. Attorney-Specific Authorization Requirements For legal requests: Use the appropriate Cleveland Clinic authorization for the relevant facility. Clearly identify the recipient law firm. Specify the requested records and applicable date range. State the purpose of disclosure where requested. Include the required signature and date. Follow the facility form for sensitive information. Cleveland Clinic’s Ohio authorization excludes psychotherapy notes, which require separate authorization. Do not assume that all Cleveland Clinic facilities use identical sensitive-record checkboxes or signature procedures. Ensuring Secure Data Handling Cleveland Clinic provides secure electronic options, MyChart access, fax submission, and facility-specific submission channels. Codes Health operates a HIPAA-compliant platform and provides secure document storage and electronic authorization workflows. Streamlining Medical Record Retrieval for Legal Needs Managing Cleveland Clinic requests across facilities can create administrative complexity, particularly when a client has treatment involving central Ohio facilities, Akron General, and Florida providers. Codes Health combines medical-record-focused AI processing with human verification to deliver high-precision analysis for legal teams. For Filevine users , Codes Health is available inside Filevine. Legal teams can submit requests from the case file, track status updates, communicate with the Codes Health team, and receive completed records and billing information without leaving the Filevine project. Ensuring Completeness and Accuracy of Your Retrieved Records Receiving records is only part of the retrieval process. Checking completeness can help identify missing documentation before demand preparation, expert review, or litigation deadlines. What to Do if Records Are Incomplete Common completeness issues: Treatment gaps between documented appointments and billing records Missing imaging files Lab results referenced in notes but not included Billing entries without corresponding treatment documentation Resolution steps: Submit a focused follow-up request identifying the missing material Reference records showing that additional documentation should exist Request appropriate custodian documentation when necessary Document unresolved gaps for the case file The Importance of Thorough Review Quality control checklist upon receipt: Requested date ranges are covered Requested record types are included Pages are legible and complete Patient identifiers are consistent Chronology is reasonably complete Codes Health’s Missing Record Review cross-references the available medical history to identify potential gaps in the record collection process. Visit Codes Health . Cost Considerations Ohio 2026 Maximum Third-Party Fees: For requests made by someone other than the patient or a qualifying patient representative, the Ohio Department of Health’s 2026 Medical Records Price Index lists maximum charges of: Initial records-search fee: $24.58 Pages 1 to 10: $1.62 per page Pages 11 to 50: $0.84 per page Pages 51 and higher: $0.33 per page Qualifying X-ray, MRI, or CAT scan data on paper or film: $2.62 per page Actual allowable postage may also be charged.
